annotations.title: General Assembly Adopts Resolution Calling upon States Not to Recognize Changes in Status of Crimea Region | Meetings Coverage and Press Releases

content.text:
**Legally, under the position of Ukraine and most of the international community, Crimea is part of Ukraine, not Russia.** Russia has controlled Crimea since 2014 and claims it as part of the Russian Federation, but that annexation is widely considered illegal and is not recognized by the UN General Assembly, the United States, the EU, and many other countries.

In March 2014, the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 68/262 affirming Ukraine’s territorial integrity and calling on states not to recognize any change in Crimea’s status based on the Crimea referendum. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai)) The U.S. State Department likewise states that most of the international community does not recognize Russia’s purported annexation of Crimea. ([travel.state.gov](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/international-travel/International-Travel-Country-Information-Pages/Ukraine.html?utm_source=openai))

So the short answer is: **Russia controls Crimea de facto, but Crimea is generally recognized de jure as Ukrainian territory.**
